pr_title: Add gRPC standard headers to known headers
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/24701

Before:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/303201/89728669-271cef00-da83-11ea-98ed-ef4346112a88.png)

After:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/303201/89728711-75ca8900-da83-11ea-84ea-c18375adce2c.png)

There are also small performance improvements. gRPC headers are get and set in header collections using fast checks. They don't fallback to using the unknown dictionary collection.

issue_context.title: Add common gRPC headers to known headers
issue_context.body:
Strings are a big contributor to allocations in gRPC benchmarks. Allocations are coming from parsing request header name/value as strings.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/303201/89707725-f1193580-d9c4-11ea-84b2-f8c2cf1bb6c7.png)

A simple way to avoid these allocations, as well as speedup setting them in header collections, is to add the common gRPC headers to known headers. Note that HttpClient as already added similar special knowledge of gRPC headers to improve performance on the client.

Request headers:
* grpc-encoding
* grpc-accept-encoding
* grpc-timeout

Response headers:
* grpc-encoding

Response trailers:
* grpc-status
* grpc-message

These are known headers from the gRPC HTTP/2 spec - https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/doc/PROTOCOL-HTTP2.md
comments: If we did this then the gRPC headers would show up in public API on https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.net.http.headers.headernames?view=aspnetcore-3.1

review_comments:
What do you think about splitting HttpRequestHeaders into Http1RequestHeaders and Http2RequestHeaders? If we include the pseudo-header fields, there are now 9 request header fields in HttpRequestHeaders that I wouldn't expect to be used with HTTP/1.x (though maybe grpc-web means the gRPC headers are also common over HTTP/1.x now).

I'm concerned that using the same HttpRequestHeaders class for HTTP/1.x and HTTP/2 and adding too many HTTP/2-specific headers will slow down HTTP/1.x unnecessarily. We already have 4 HTTP/2 pseudo-header fields in `requestPrimaryHeaders`. TryGetValueFast will check if the requested header name matches these primary headers before other header names of the same length. Any extra header fields waste memory and slow down methods like Clear, TryGetValueFast, Append, etc...

I think that would be a good improvement. I don't know if there will be time for .NET 5.

On primary headers: the HTTP/2 pseudo-headers can probably be removed from primary headers. Pseudo-headers are sent in HEADERS frame as static table indexes. They'll use the upcoming optimizations here: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/24730
Are these exact header names used for both HTTP/2 gRPC and gRPC-Web? If so, I guess these warrant being in a possible Http1RequestHeaders dictionary anyway.

gRPC-Web headers are the same, and gRPC-Web is usable in HTTP/1.1 and 2. So yes it is useful for them to be in a potential Http1RequestHeaders.

The only HTTP/2 specific headers are the pseudo ones.
